Preheat the oven to 190 °C; line a tray: Knead all the ingredients for 3–4 minutes.
Shape walnut-sized meatballs and flatten them slightly.
Bake for 18–20 minutes until completely cooked inside; when cut in half there should be no pink.
Let cool and break into pieces your baby can hold.
Even after age one, use very little salt or none at all.
Cooked meatballs: 48 hours in the fridge, 1 month in the freezer.
3 tablespoons small pasta (orzo, stars, etc.)
Half a cup finely chopped vegetables (your choice)
1 tablespoon grated fresh kashar or lor cheese
Boil the pasta in plenty of unsalted water for 2 minutes longer than the packet says, until soft.
At the same time, steam or cook the vegetables in a little water for 8–10 minutes.
Drain the pasta; mix with the vegetables and olive oil.
Add the cheese and stir while hot until melted.
Kashar can be salty; prefer low-salt lor or fresh cheese.
24 hours in the fridge.
3 tablespoons wholemeal flour
2 tablespoons very finely chopped or grated vegetables (your choice)
Whisk the egg, flour and milk until smooth.
Stir in the vegetables; rest for 5 minutes.
Lightly grease a non-stick pan with butter and pour in 2 tablespoons of batter.
Cook each side over a low heat for 2–3 minutes until the centre is fully cooked.
When lukewarm, cut into strips and serve.
If you blanch spinach for 1 minute and squeeze it first, the crêpe will be softer.
24 hours in the fridge; warm gently in a pan.
Baked vegetable mücver (fritters)
1 medium vegetable (your choice), grated
2 tablespoons crumbled lor cheese
1 tablespoon finely chopped dill
Preheat the oven to 190 °C; grease a muffin tin or line a tray with paper.
Squeeze the liquid out of the grated vegetables thoroughly with muslin.
Divide the mixture into the tin, or spoon flat rounds onto the tray.
Bake for 20–22 minutes until golden on top and firm in the middle; let cool, then serve.
Baking instead of frying reduces the fat content.
48 hours in the fridge; can be frozen.
2 tablespoons finely chopped vegetables (your choice)
Melt the butter in a pan and soften the vegetables for 3–4 minutes.
Whisk the egg with the milk and pour into the pan.
Cover and cook over a low heat for 3–4 minutes until the top is completely set.
Flip and cook 1 more minute; when lukewarm, cut into strips.
Chop mushrooms very finely; their slippery texture can get stuck in the throat.
Fruit yogurt bowl
4 tablespoons full-fat plain yogurt
3 tablespoons mashed or finely chopped fruit (your choice)
1 tablespoon fine rolled oats
A pinch of cinnamon (optional)
Wash the fruit; mash banana and pear with a fork, cut strawberries and peaches into small pieces.
Cut blueberries in halves or quarters.
Put the yogurt in a bowl and add the fruit and oats.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and serve immediately.
Always cut small round fruits (blueberries, grapes) before giving them.
Don’t add honey; even after 12 months, a no-sugar habit is recommended.
Potato and vegetable mash
Half a cup vegetables (your choice)
2 tablespoons milk, or breast milk/formula
Peel and dice the potato and boil for 10 minutes.
Add the vegetables and cook 8 more minutes until both are soft.
Drain and mash with a fork together with the butter and milk.
According to age, leave it slightly lumpy or smooth, and serve lukewarm.
Don’t give cow’s milk as a drink before 12 months; it can be used in small amounts in food.
Semolina and vegetable porridge
2 tablespoons grated vegetables (your choice)
Cook the vegetables in the water for 7–8 minutes until soft.
Sprinkle in the semolina like rain, stirring constantly.
Keep stirring so it doesn’t go lumpy and cook for 4–5 minutes until thick.
Add the butter and let it cool.
Semolina is made from wheat and contains gluten.
Eat straight away; it stiffens as it stands.
3 tablespoons couscous
Sauté the vegetables in olive oil for 5–6 minutes until soft.
Add the couscous and toss for 1 minute.
Add the hot water, cover and turn off the heat.
Leave to steam for 10 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve lukewarm.
Couscous contains wheat.
Quinoa with vegetables
2 tablespoons quinoa
Rinse the quinoa well in a fine sieve, rubbing it under plenty of water to remove the bitterness.
Put the quinoa and water in a pot; once boiling, cook over a low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the vegetables and cook 8–10 more minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are soft.
Add the olive oil and mash according to age.
Quinoa is gluten-free; a good grain alternative for variety.
50 g chicken breast or thigh
1 dessert spoon rice or orzo
Boil the chicken in the water; once boiling, skim off the foam and cook for 20 minutes.
Remove the chicken and shred it finely.
Add the potato, vegetables and rice to the broth and cook for 20 minutes.
Return the chicken; blend or leave in pieces according to age.
Before giving the soup to your baby, check its temperature on the inside of your wrist.
3 tablespoons red lentils
1 small vegetable (your choice)
1 tablespoon finely chopped onion
Wash and drain the lentils; chop the vegetable small.
Soften the onion in butter for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, vegetable and water; once boiling, cook over a low heat for 25 minutes.
Blend and adjust the consistency with boiled water.
For children over one year old, you can add a few drops of lemon when serving.
3 tablespoons very finely chopped vegetables (your choice)
2 tablespoons lor cheese
Preheat the oven to 180 °C; grease a 6-hole mini muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs with the milk; add the vegetables and lor cheese.
Fill the moulds two-thirds full.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until a cocktail stick comes out clean.
Leave in the tin for 5 minutes, then turn out and serve warm.
As finger food, it supports your baby’s self-feeding.
Half a cup homemade or shop-bought egg noodles
1 tablespoon strained yogurt
Boil the noodles in unsalted water for 10–12 minutes until soft.
Cook the vegetables in butter, covered, for 6–7 minutes.
Mix the drained noodles with the vegetables.
When lukewarm, serve with yogurt; cut long noodles into small pieces.
Cutting long pasta reduces the risk of choking.
Baked chicken and vegetable meatballs
100 g minced chicken
3 tablespoons finely grated vegetables (your choice), squeezed
2 tablespoons rolled oats
Knead all the ingredients and rest in the fridge for 10 minutes.
With wet hands, shape small flat meatballs and arrange on a lined tray.
Bake for 18–20 minutes until completely white inside.
Let cool and serve in pieces your baby can hold.
Minced chicken must always be thoroughly cooked inside.
